verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              ततः पुनरमेयात्मा केशवोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत् । कृतसंकल्पमायान्तं वधे कर्णस्य भारत ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O Bharata, then again did Kesava of magnanimous heart address the following words to Arjuna, who was proceeding resolutely to slay Karna.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य सप्तदशाहानि वर्तमानस्य भारत । विनाशस्यातिघोरस्य नरवारणवाजिनाम् ॥२॥
verses.english: Today, O Bharata, is the seventeenth day of this horrible carnage of men, elephants and horses.

verses.sanskrit: भूत्वा हि विपुला सेना तावकानां परैः सह । अन्योन्यं समरं प्राप्य किञ्चिच्छेषा विशांपते ॥३॥
verses.english: O sovereign, at first your own troops and those of the hostile party were a legion, but being engaged in fight there have been left but a small remnant.

verses.sanskrit: भूत्वा वै कौरवाः पार्थ प्रभूतगजवाजिनः । त्वां वै शत्रुं समासाद्य विनष्टा रणमूर्धनि ॥४॥
verses.english: Though the Kauravas had, at the outset, numerous steeds and elephants, yet they have been routed on the field as they had to face yourself as their foe.

verses.sanskrit: एते ते पृथिवीपालाः सृञ्जयाश्च समागताः । त्वां समासाद्य दुर्धर्षं पाण्डवाश्च व्यवस्थिताः ॥५॥
verses.english: These potentates and these united forces of the Srinjayas and these Pandavas have been successful in holding their ground, only because they have such an unflinching leader in you.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चालैः पाण्डवैर्मत्स्यैः कारूषैश्चेदिभिः सह । त्वया गुप्तैरमित्रघ्नैः कृतः शत्रुगणक्षयः ॥६॥
verses.english: O destroyer of foes, being under your protection, the Panchala, Pandava, Matsya, Karusa and Chedis hosts have been sweeping away the hostile army.

verses.sanskrit: को हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं कौरवांस्तात संयुगे । अन्यत्र पाण्डवान्युद्धे त्वया गुप्तान्महारथान् ॥७॥
verses.english: O Sire, who else could have vanquished the combined army of the Kauravas had not the valiant Pandavas been fighting under your aegis?

verses.sanskrit: शक्तस्त्वं हि रणे जेतुं ससुरासुरमानुषान् । त्रीन् लोकान्समरे युक्तान्किं पुनः कौरवं बलम् ॥८॥
verses.english: What need I speak of defeating the Kauravas? Single-handed you can vanquish in battle the Asuras, celestials and human beings of the three worlds put together.

verses.sanskrit: भगदत्तं च राजानं कोऽन्यः शक्तस्त्वया विना । जेतुं पुरुषशार्दूल योऽपि स्याद्वासवोपमः ॥९॥
verses.english: O mighty one, who else, excepting yourself, could have conquered Bhagadatta in fight, even were he powerful like Vasava himself.

verses.sanskrit: तथेमां विपुलां सेनां गुप्तां पार्थ त्वयाऽनघ । न शेकुः पार्थिवाः सर्वे चक्षुर्भिरपि वीक्षितुम् ॥१०॥
verses.english: O holy Partha, no mortal could even gaze upon this vast army, being as they were, under your protection.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव सततं पार्थ रक्षिताभ्यां त्वया रणे । धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिभ्यां भीष्मद्रोणौ निपातितौ ॥११॥
verses.english: O Partha, Dhristadyumna and Shikhandi had succeeded in slaying Drona and Bhishma, only because you protected them in battle.

verses.sanskrit: को हि शक्तो रणे पार्थ भारतानां महारथौ । भीष्मद्रोणौ युधा जेतुं शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमौ ॥१२॥
verses.english: Or, O Partha, who else could have conquered in battle those most eminent warriors of the Bharata race-Drona and Bhishma, endued with the prowess of a Sakra.

verses.sanskrit: को हि शान्तनवं भीष्मं द्रोणं वैकर्तनं कृपम् । द्रौणिं च सौमदत्तिं च कृतवर्माणमेव च ॥१३॥
verses.english: O most powerful one, who else but you could defeat those formidable leaders of Aksouhinis, those unflinching and invincible heroes, Bhishma-son of Shantanu, Drona, Vaikartana, Kripa and Drona's son and King Duryodhana himself, all united together and adepts in wielding arms.

verses.sanskrit: सैन्धवं मद्रराजानं राजानं च सुयोधनम् । वीरान् कृतास्त्रान् समरे सर्वानेवानिवर्तिनः ॥१४॥
अक्षौहिणीपतीनुग्रान्संहतान् युद्धदुर्मदान् । त्वामृते पुरुषव्याघ्र जेतुं शक्तः पुमानिह ॥१५॥
श्रेण्यश्च बहुलाः क्षीणाः प्रदीर्णाश्वरथद्विपाः । नानाजनपदाश्चोग्राः क्षत्रियाणाममर्षिणाम् ॥१६॥
verses.english: Numerous detachments of (hostile) soldiers have been extirpated; their cars, horses and elephants have been cut down (by you), as also numbers of indignant and impetuous Kshatriyas hailing from various provinces.

verses.sanskrit: गोवासदासमीयानां वसातीनां च भारत । प्राच्यानां वाटधानानां भोजानां चाभिमानिनाम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: O Bharata (lo) the forces of the Gobasas, the Dasmiyas, Basatis, the Easterners, the Batadhanas and the sensitive Bhojas and of other Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, with their best horses and elephants, have all been slain confronting you and Bhima (in battle).

verses.sanskrit: उदीर्णाश्वगजा सेना सर्वक्षत्रस्य भारत । त्वां समासाद्य निधनं गता भीमं च भारत ॥१८॥
उग्राश्च भीमकर्माणस्तुषारा यवनाः खशाः । दार्वाभिसारा दरदाः शका माठरतङ्गणाः ॥१९॥
verses.english: The Tusharas, the Yavanas, the Khashas, the Darbabhisaras, the Daradas, the Shakas, the Ramathas, the Tanganas, the Andhraks, the Pulindas, all of fierce temperament and awful deeds and the Kiratas of formidable prowess and the Mlechhas, the mountain tribes and the people inhabiting the sea coasts, all of whom are very powerful unflinching in battle and wielders of maces, have gathered round the standard of the Kurus and been fighting hard for Suyodhana. And none else but you, O scorcher of foes, could defeat them in battle.

verses.sanskrit: आन्ध्रकाश्च पुलिंदाश्च किराताश्चोग्रविक्रमाः । म्लेच्छाश्च पर्वतीयाश्च सागरानूपवासिनः ॥२०॥
संरंभिणो युद्धशौण्डा बलिनो दण्डपाणयः । एते सुयोधनस्यार्थे संरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह ॥२१॥
न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परन्तप । धार्तराष्ट्रमुदग्रं हि व्यूढं दृष्ट्वा महद्बलम् ॥२२॥
यदि त्वं न भवेस्त्राता प्रतीयात्को नु मानवः । तत्सागरमिवोद्धूतं रजसा संवृतं बलम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: If you had not come to the rescue who else could advance against the mighty troops of the Dhartarashtras arrayed in battle order?

verses.sanskrit: विदार्य पाण्डवैः क्रुद्धैस्त्वया गुप्तैर्हतं विभो । मागधानामधिपतिर्जयत्सेनो महाबलः ॥२४॥
verses.english: Ten mighty Jayatsena, the king of the Magadhas, was slain in battle by Abhimanyu these seven days past.
verses.bhavadeepa: यदि त्वं त्राता न भवेस्तर्हि तद्धार्तराष्ट्रं बलं कोऽनुप्रतीयादिति सम्बन्धः ॥२३॥

verses.sanskrit: अद्य सप्तैव चाहानि हतः संख्येऽभिमन्युना । ततो दशसहस्राणि गजानां भीमकर्मणाम् ॥२५॥
जघान गदया भीमस्तस्य राज्ञः परिच्छदम् । ततोऽन्येऽभिहता नागा रथाश्च शतशो बलात् ॥२६॥
verses.english: Ten thousand powerful elephants, forming the king's retinue, were then struck down by Bhimasena with his mace. Later on hundreds of other elephants and charioteer fell through Bhima's powerful hands.

verses.sanskrit: तदेवं समरे पार्थ वर्तमाने महाभये । भीमसेनं समासाद्य त्वां च पाण्डव कौरवाः ॥२७॥
verses.english: Therefore, O Partha, in the course of this terrible battle the Kauravas, along with their steeds, cars and elephants, have fallen victims of Death no sooner they encountered Bhimasena and yourself.

verses.sanskrit: सवाजिरथमातङ्गा मृत्युलोकमितो गताः । तथा सेनामुखे तत्र निहते पार्थ पाण्डवैः ॥२८॥
भीष्मः प्रासृजदुग्राणि शरजालानि मारिष । स चेदिकाशिपञ्चालान् करूषान् मत्स्यकेकयान् ॥२९॥
verses.english: O Partha, the van of the Kaurava host on being slain by the Pandavas, Bhishma shot forth showers of deadly arrows.

verses.sanskrit: शरैः प्रच्छाद्य निधनमनयत्परमास्त्रवित् । तस्य चापच्युतैर्बाणैः परदेहविदारणैः ॥३०॥
verses.english: Skilled in the use of celestial weapons he covered the Chedis, the Kashis, the Panchalas, the Karushas, the Matsyas and the Kaikeyas, with his arrows and slew them to a man.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्णमाकाशमभवद्रुक्मपुंखैरजिह्मगैः । हन्याद्रथसहस्त्राणि एकैकेनैव मुष्टिना ॥३१॥
verses.english: The atmosphere became thick with goldfeathered, straight-shot deadly arrows, that were discharged from his bow.

verses.sanskrit: लक्षं नरद्विपान्हत्वा समेतान्समहाबलान् । गत्या दशम्या ते गत्वा जघ्नुर्वाजिरथद्विपान् ॥३२॥
verses.english: Discharging flights of shafts at a time he struck down thousands of charioteers. He killed in all a hundred thousand powerful men and elephants.

verses.sanskrit: हित्वा नवगतीर्दुष्टाः स बाणानाहवेऽत्यजत् । दिनानि दश भीष्मेण निघ्नता तावकं बलम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: The shafts he shot during the battle did not take any of the nine wrong courses, but flying direct through the tenth (and the approved) course destroyed many steeds, cars and elephants.

verses.sanskrit: शून्याः कृता रथोपस्था हताश्च गजवाजिनः । दर्शयित्त्वाऽऽत्मनो रूपं रुद्रोपेन्द्रसमं युधि ॥३४॥
verses.english: Massacring the (Pandava) troops for ten days together, Bhishma rendered the terraces of many a car empty and slew numberless elephants and steeds.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डवानामनीकानि प्रगृह्यासौ व्यशातयत् । विनिघ्नन्पृथिवीपालांश्चेदिपञ्चालकेकयान् ॥३५॥
verses.english: Assuming the form, of Rudra or that of Upendra in battle, he afflicted the Pandava detachment and played a havoc with them.

verses.sanskrit: अदहत्पाण्डवीं सेनां रथाश्वगजसंकुलाम् । मज्जन्तमप्लवे मन्दमुज्जिहीर्षुः सुयोधनम् ॥३६॥
verses.english: The wicked Suyodhana, bereft of a cause was about to be drowned in the sea of misfortune and with the view of rescuing him Bhishma slaughtered the rulers of the Chedis, the Panchalas and the Kaikeyas and caused a great carnage amongst the Pandava army teeming with cars, steeds with elephants.

verses.sanskrit: तथा चरन्तं समरे तपन्तमिव भास्करम् । पदातिकोटिसाहस्त्राः प्रवरायुधपाणयः ॥३७॥
verses.english: As he careered in battle, resplendent like the Sun himself neither the innumerable infantry of the Srinjayas, all well armed, nor the other rulers of the earth were even able to look at him. Yet the Pandava troops with all their resources made a giant effort against the victorious Bhishma who was thus careering in the battle.

verses.sanskrit: न शेकुः सृञ्जया द्रष्टुं तथैवान्ये महीक्षितः । विचरन्तं तथा तं तु संग्रामे जितकाशिनम् ॥३८॥
सर्वोद्यमेन महता पाण्डवान्समभिद्रवत् । स तु विद्राव्य समरे पाण्डवान्सृञ्जयानपि ॥३९॥
एक एव रणे भीष्म एकवीरत्वमागतः । तं शिखण्डी समासाद्य त्वया गुप्तो महाव्रतम् ॥४०॥
verses.english: Indeed he had achieved an unrivalled heroism in the field, having routed the Pandavas and the Srinjayas all single-handed in battle.

verses.sanskrit: जघान पुरुषव्याघ्रं शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः । स एष पतितः शेते शरतल्पे पितामहः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Being under your powerful protection Sikhandin encountered him and with his straight shafts slew that foremost of men. O mighty one, as the Asura Vritra courted his death obtaining Vasava for his foe, so having obtained you (as his foe) there lies on a bed of arrows that grandsire (wrapt in eternal sleep).

verses.sanskrit: त्वां प्राप्य पुरुषव्याघ्रं वृत्रः प्राप्येव वासवम् । द्रोणः पञ्चदिनान्युग्रो विधम्य रिपुवाहिनीम् ॥४२॥
कृत्वा व्यूहमभेद्यं च पातयित्वा महारथान् । जयद्रथस्य समरे कृत्वा रक्षां महारथः ॥४३॥
verses.english: The violent Drona having arranged his troops in an impenetrable array has slain the army of the enemies and many a mighty charioteer for five days together. That valiant charioteer having protected Jayadratha in battle committed a havoc amongst the hostile army during the nocturnal fight, like the fierce Destroyer himself.

verses.sanskrit: अन्तकप्रतिमश्चोग्रो रात्रियुद्धेऽदहत्प्रजाः । दग्ध्वा योधाञ्छरैर्वीरो भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान् ॥४४॥
धृष्टद्युम्नं समासाद्य स गतः परमां गतिम् । यदि वाऽद्य भवान्युद्धे सूतपुत्रमुखान्रथान् ॥४५॥
verses.english: Having with his arrows killed numerous warriors that valiant and chivalrous son of Bharadvaja, at last attained highest and on encountering Dhristadyumna.

verses.sanskrit: नावारयिष्यः संग्रामे न स्म द्रोणो व्यनङ्क्ष्यत । भवता तु बलं सर्वं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य वारितम् ॥४६॥
verses.english: If you had not held at day Suta's son and other charioteers in the battle that day, then Drona would never have been slain.

verses.sanskrit: ततो द्रोणो हतो युद्धे पार्षतेन धनञ्जयः । एवं वा को रणे कुर्यात्त्वदन्यः क्षत्रियो युधि ॥४७॥
verses.english: O Dhananjaya, you kept engaged the entire Dhartarashtra forces and thus it was that the son of Prishata could slay Drona.

verses.sanskrit: यादृशं ते कृतं पार्थ जयद्रथवधं प्रति । निवार्य सेनां महतीं हत्वा शूरांश्च पार्थिवान् ॥४८॥
verses.english: O Partha, who else among the Kshatriyas but you, could have achieved such feats (of as material strength), you did when overthrowing Jayadratha?

verses.sanskrit: निहतः सैन्धवो राजा त्वयाऽस्त्रबलतेजसा । आश्चर्यं सिन्धुराजस्य वधं जानन्ति पार्थिवाः ॥४९॥
verses.english: Having thwarted the vast host and slain numerous valiant kings you, with the strength of your weapons, have slain the ruler of the Sindhus.

verses.sanskrit: अनाश्चर्यं हि तत्त्वत्तस्त्वं हि पार्थ महारथः । त्वां हि प्राप्य रणे क्षत्रमेकाहादिति भारत ॥५०॥
verses.english: O Partha, to the mortals the slaughter of the ruler of the Sindhus seem to be exceedingly strange, but to you it is no wonder, as you are an eminent charioteer.

verses.sanskrit: नश्यमानमहं युक्तं मन्येयमिति मे मतिः । सेयं पार्थचमूर्घोरा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य संयुगे ॥५१॥
verses.english: O Bharata, methinks, it would not appear impossible even if all the Kshatriyas were to be exterminated in the course of a day, with you for their adversary in the field.
verses.bhavadeepa: त्वां हीति । क्षणेन सर्वं भस्मीकर्तुं समर्थं त्वां प्राप्य एकाहान्नश्यमानं क्षत्रं युक्तं बलवत्तरं मन्येयं जानीयां क्षणेन नाश्यमपि पूर्णैकाहपर्यन्तं स्थायित्वादिति भावः । सार्धः ॥५०॥

verses.sanskrit: हतसर्वस्ववीरा हि भीष्मद्रोणौ यदा हतौ । शीर्णप्रवरयोधाऽद्य हतवाजिरथद्विपा ॥५२॥
verses.english: O Partha, now that Bhishma and Drona are slain, the fierce Dhritarashtra force may well be regarded to have lost all their heroes.

verses.sanskrit: हीना सूर्येन्दुनक्षत्रैर्द्योरिवाभाति भारती । विध्वस्ता हि रणे पार्थ सेनेयं भीमविक्रम ॥५३॥
verses.english: With their chef and foremost warriors slain, with their horses, chariots and elephants struck down, the Bharata army look like the welkin bereft of the Sun, the Moon and the Stars.

verses.sanskrit: आसुरीव पुरा सेना शक्रस्येव पराक्रमैः । तेषां हतावशिष्टास्तु सन्ति पञ्च महारथाः ॥५४॥
verses.english: O Partha, as the Asura hosts were routed by the prowess of Sakra in days of yore, so yonder host of terrible prowess have been vanquished by you.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वत्थामा कृतवर्मा कर्णो मद्राधिपः कृपः । तांस्त्वमद्य नरव्याघ्र हत्वा पञ्च महारथान् ॥५५॥
verses.english: Besides the slain there are now left only five mighty charioteers, Ashvatthama, Kritavarma, Karna, Shalya-the ruler of Madra and Kripa.

verses.sanskrit: हतामित्रः प्रयच्छोर्वी राज्ञे सद्वीपपत्तनाम् । साकाशजलपातालां सपर्वतमहावनाम् ॥५६॥
verses.english: O mightiest of men, by killing those five eminent charioteers today may you get rid of all foes and bestow this earth with all its islands, cities and seas to King Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्नोत्वमितवीर्यश्रीरद्य पार्थो वसुंधराम् । एतां पुरा विष्णुरिव हत्वा दैतेयदानवान् ॥५७॥
verses.english: As Vishnu, in days of yore, made a gift of the three worlds to Sakra after overthrowing the Daityas and the Danavas, so may you bestow the Earth on the king after slaying the Kauravas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रयच्छ मेदिनीं राज्ञे शक्रायैव हरिर्यथा । अद्य मोदन्तु पञ्चाला निहतेष्वरिषु त्वया । विष्णुना निहतेष्वेव दानवेयेषु देवताः ॥५८॥
verses.english: On their enemies being slain, let the Panchalas rejoice today as did the celestials on the occasion of Vishnu's exterminating the Danavas.

verses.sanskrit: यदि वा द्विपदां श्रेष्ठं द्रोणं मानयतो गुरुम् । अश्वत्थाम्नि कृपा तेऽस्ति कृपे वाचार्यगौरवात् ॥५९॥
verses.english: If out of respect for that illustrious personage, your preceptor Drona, you feel sympathy for Ashvatthama, if again out of reverence due to a preceptor, you are kindly disposed towards Kripa. If out of high regard for your material relatives you do not dispatch Kritavarman today to the regions of Pluto in encountering him. If, O lotus-eyed one, encountering your mother's brother, Shalya, the king of Madras, out of mere compassion, you do not deign to strike him down. Do you, O mighty one, with your sharp shafts hasten to slay that wretched Karna today who, at heart, cherishes utmost hatred for the sons of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: अत्यन्तापचितान्बन्धून्मानयन्मातृबान्धवान् । कृतवर्माणमासाद्य न नेष्यसि यमक्षयम् ॥६०॥
भ्रातरं मातुरासाद्य शल्यं मद्रजनाधिपम् । यदि त्वमरविन्दाक्ष दयावान्न जिघांससि ॥६१॥
इमं पापमतिं क्षुद्रमत्यन्तं पाण्डवान्प्रति । कर्णमद्य नरश्रेष्ठ जह्याः सुनिशितैः शरैः ॥६२॥
एतत्ते सुकृतं कर्म नात्र किंचन युज्यते । वयमप्यनुजानीमो नात्र दोषोऽस्ति कश्चन ॥६३॥
verses.english: It is your noblest duty; nor is there any impropriety in it; we all assent to it and there is no guilt in that.

verses.sanskrit: दहने यत्सपुत्राया निशि मातुस्तवानघ । द्यूतार्थे यच्च युष्मासु प्रावर्तत सुयोधनः ॥६४॥
verses.english: O sinless one, in that attempt to burn your mother with all her children during the night and the behaviour that Suyodhana bore towards you during the play at dice, that wretched Karna lay at the bottom of all.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य सर्वस्य दुष्टात्मा कर्णो वै मूलमित्युत । कर्णाद्धि मन्यते त्राणं नित्यमेव सुयोधनः ॥६५॥
ततो मामपि संरब्धो निग्रहीतुं प्रचक्रमे । स्थिरा बुद्धिर्नरेन्द्रस्य धार्तराष्ट्रस्य मानद ॥६६॥
verses.english: Suyodhana has ever a firm conviction that it is Karna alone who will help him out (of this scrape). That is why he has been filled with rage and tries also to afflict me.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णः पार्थान् रणे सर्वान्विजेष्यति न संशयः । कर्णमाश्रित्य कौन्तेय धार्तराष्ट्रेण विग्रहः ॥६७॥
verses.english: O giver of honours, it is the firm belief of the royal Dhartarashtras that Karna will, to a certainty, slay all the Parthas in battle.

verses.sanskrit: रोचितो भवता सार्धं जानताऽपि बलं तव । कर्णो हि भाषते नित्यमहं पार्थान्समागतान् ॥६८॥
verses.english: O son of Kunti, it is through having secured the aid of Karna that Dhritarashtra's son has ventured to fight with you, though he is full well aware of your prowess.

verses.sanskrit: वासुदेवं च दाशार्हं विजेष्यामि महारथम् । प्रोत्साहयन्दुरात्मानं धार्तराष्ट्रं सुदुर्मतिम् ॥६९॥
verses.english: Karna also often says that, “I will conquer the assembled Parthas and Vasudeva, that valiant charioteer of Dasharha's race. roars

verses.sanskrit: समितौ गर्जते कर्णस्तमद्य जहि भारत । यच्च युष्मासु पापं वै धार्तराष्ट्रः प्रयुक्तवान् ॥७०॥
verses.english: O Bharata, that wicked Karna thus always in the court (of the Kurus) of Dhritarashtra. Do you, therefore, slay him today.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र सर्वत्र दुष्टात्मा कर्णः पापमतिर्मुखम् । यच्च तद्धार्तराष्ट्रस्य क्रूरैः षड्भिर्महारथैः ॥७१॥
verses.english: It is the profane and malignant Karna who is mainly responsible for all the evils that have been done to you by Dhritarashtra's son.

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यं निहतं वीरं सौभद्रमृषभेक्षणम् । द्रोणद्रौणिकृपान्वीरान्कर्षयन्तं नरर्षभान् ॥७२॥
verses.english: I have seen the valiant son of Subhadra, of lustrous eyes, fall at the hands of six heartless charioteers belonging to the Dhritarasthra force. Harassing mighty heroes like Drona, Drona's son and Kripa and others, he divested elephants of their riders and mighty charioteers of their cars. Abhimanyu of mighty neck, the pride and the glory of both the Kurus and the Vrisnis, made also the steeds bereft of their riders and the infantry, their arms and life. Overthrowing the hostile files and harassing many powerful charioteers, he has packed off numbers of men and steeds and elephants to the gates of Pluto. O friend, by truth I swear unto you that I am burning at the thought that while Subhadra's son was thus advancing, striking down with his arrows the hostile force, even then, O lord Partha, the malevolent Karna, unable to withstand him in a face to face fight, had been engaged in acts of hostility to that heroic Abhimanyu. Mangled with the arrows of Subhadra's son, rendered senseless and bathed in blood.

verses.sanskrit: निर्मनुष्यांश्च मातंगान्विरथांश्च महारथान् । व्यश्वारोहांश्च तुरगान्पत्तीन्व्यायुधजीविनः ॥७३॥
कुर्वन्तमृषभस्कंधं कुरुवृष्णियशस्करम् । विधमन्तमनीकानि व्यथयन्तं महारथान् ॥७४॥
मनुष्यवाजिमातङ्गान्प्राहिण्वन्तं यमक्षयम् । शरैः सौभद्रमायान्तं दहन्तमिव वाहिनीम् ॥७५॥
तन्मे दहति गात्राणि सखे सत्येन ते शपे । यत्तत्रापि च दुष्टात्मा कर्णोऽभ्यद्रुह्यत प्रभो ॥७६॥
अशक्नुवंश्चाभिमन्योः कर्णः स्थातुं रणेऽग्रतः । सौभद्रशरनिर्भिन्नो विसंज्ञः शोणितोक्षितः ॥७७॥
निःश्वसन् क्रोधसंदीप्तो विमुखः सायकार्दितः । अपयानकृतोत्साहो निराशश्चापि जीविते ॥७८॥
verses.english: Karna became highly enraged and drew heavy breaths, till at last covered with shafts he thought of turning away from the field. Heartily wished to bear a retreat, but finding no means of egress of doing so, giving up all the while his hopes of life.

verses.sanskrit: तस्थौ सुविह्वलः संख्ये प्रहारजनितश्रमः । अथ द्रोणस्य समरे तत्कालसदृशं तदा ॥७९॥
verses.english: Exhausted and stupefied with the wounds received, he had to roam about in the field. At last hearing the opportune, though wanton, words of Drona in battle, Karna cut-off Abhimanyu's bow.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा कर्णो वचः क्रूरं ततश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् । ततश्छिन्नायुधं तेन रणे पञ्च महारथाः ॥८०॥
तं चैव निकृतिप्रज्ञाः प्राहरञ्छरवृष्टिभिः । तस्मिन्विनिहते वीरे सर्वेषां दुःखमाविशत् ॥८१॥
verses.english: On his bow being thus cut asunder in that battle, five mighty charioteers of blunt conscience slew him with showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: प्राहसत्स तु दुष्टात्मा कर्णः स च सुयोधनः । यच्च कर्णोऽब्रवीत्कृष्णां सभायां परुषं वचः ॥८२॥
verses.english: On the hero being thus slain all were touched at heart. Only that wicked-hearted Karna and Suyodhana laughed.

verses.sanskrit: प्रमुखे पाण्डवेयानां कुरूणां च नृशंसवत् । विनष्टाः पाण्डवाः कृष्णे शाश्वतं नरकं गताः ॥८३॥
verses.english: (Verily you remember) the vile epithets that Karna so cruelly flung towards Krishna in the (Kuru) court before both the Kurus the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: पतिमन्यं पृथुश्रोणि वृणीष्व मृदुभाषिणि । एषा त्वं धृतराष्ट्रस्य दासीभूता निवेशनम् ॥८४॥
प्रविशारालपद्माक्षि न सन्ति पतयस्तव । न पाण्डवाः प्रभवन्ति तव कृष्णे कथञ्चन ॥८५॥
दासभार्या च पाञ्चालि स्वयं दासी च शोभने । अद्य दुर्योधनो ह्येकः पृथिव्यां नृपतिः स्मृतः ॥८६॥
verses.english: O Princess of Panchala, you are now the wife of men that are servants and O beautiful one, yourself, a maid. Duryodhana alone is regarded as the ruler of this earth.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे चास्य महीपाला योगक्षेममुपासते । पश्येदानीं यथा भद्रे विनष्टाः पाण्डवाः समम् ॥८७॥
verses.english: Today all the other lords are engaged in helping him towards the good government of his state. Lo, O amiable one, how all the Pandavas have equally fallen, under the prowess of Dhirtarasthtra's son and have now been staring at each other.

verses.sanskrit: अन्योन्यं समुदीक्षन्ते धार्तराष्ट्रस्य तेजसा । व्यक्तं षण्ढतिला ह्येते न पुरेव निमज्जिताः ॥८८॥
प्रेष्यवच्चापि राजानमुपस्थास्यन्ति कौरवम् । इत्युक्तवानधर्मज्ञस्तदा परमदुर्मतिः ॥८९॥
verses.english: Verily these (men) are like sesame seeds without kernel and have fallen into purgatory and they will have to serve ere long that foremost of Kaurava Kings.

verses.sanskrit: पापः पापवचः कर्णः शृण्वतस्तव भारत । अद्य पापस्य तद्वाक्यं सुवर्णविकृताः शराः ॥९०॥
verses.english: O Bharata, these vile words were uttered by that sinful, debased, mischievous and unprincipled Karna at that time, in your hearing.

verses.sanskrit: शमयन्तु शिलाधौतास्त्वयास्ता जीवितच्छिदः । यानि चान्यानि दुष्टात्मा पापानि कृतवांस्त्वयि ॥९१॥
verses.english: Let your gold-plated and sharpened shafts, capable of dealing death to the living today assuage the sorrows caused by those words of effrontery.

verses.sanskrit: तान्यद्य जीवितं चास्य शमयन्तु शरास्तव । गाण्डीवप्रहितान्घोरानद्य गात्रैःस्पृशञ्छरान् ॥९२॥
verses.english: Let your shafts retaliate all the other mischief's done to you by that wicked one by slaying him.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णः स्मरतु दुष्टात्मा वचनं द्रोणभीष्मयोः। सुवर्णपुङ्खा नाराचाः शत्रुघ्ना वैद्युतप्रभाः ॥९३॥
verses.english: Let the wicked Karna feel the pangs of those deadly shafts sped from the Gandiva and remember the words of Bhishma and Drona.

verses.sanskrit: त्वयाऽस्तास्तस्य वर्माणि भित्त्वा पास्यन्ति शोणितम् । उग्रास्त्वद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता मर्म भित्त्वा महाशराः ॥९४॥
verses.english: Let the gold-feathered iron shafts, capable of dealing death to the enemies and emitting rays of lightning, sped by you go straight into the vital organs and drink his blood.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य कर्णं महावेगाः प्रेषयन्तु यमक्षयम् । अद्य हाहाकृता दीना विषण्णास्त्वच्छरार्दिताः ॥९५॥
verses.english: Let the sharp and winged arrow of irresistible force shot by your arms touch Karna to the core and dispatch him off to the den of Pluto.

verses.sanskrit: प्रपतन्तं रथात्कर्णं पश्यन्तु वसुधाधिपाः । अद्य शोणितसंमग्नं शयानं पतितं भुवि । अपविद्धायुधं कर्णं दीनाः पश्यन्तु बान्धवाः ॥९६॥
verses.english: Let the lords of this hemisphere, seeing Karna fall today from off his chariot, covered with your shafts, despondent and heart-broken, indulge themselves in grief.

verses.sanskrit: हस्तिकक्षो महानस्य भल्लेनोन्मथितस्त्वया । प्रकम्पमानः पततु भूमावपि रथध्वजः ॥९७॥
verses.english: Let the huge standard of Adhiratha's son, bearing the ensign of the elephant's rope, totter to its fall from the shots of crescent-shaped arrows.

verses.sanskrit: त्वया शरशतैश्छिन्नं रथं हेमविभूषितम् । हतयोधाश्वमुत्सृज्य भीतः शल्यः पलायताम् ॥९८॥
verses.english: Let Shalya, alarmed with the scene of his golden chariot thus scattered to the winds and his charioteer and steeds taken off with numberless darts of your arrows, deserting his empty car, beat a hasty retreat (from the field).

verses.sanskrit: त्वं चेत्कर्णसुतं पार्थ सूतपुत्रस्य पश्यतः । प्रतिज्ञावारणार्थाय निहनिष्यसि सायकैः ॥९९॥
verses.english: Partha! You honour always the meritorious people. In case, you kill Vrishasena, son of Karna before his eyes in order to keep your commitment, he will definitely remember the advice given him by Dronacharya, Bhishma and Vidura time to time under influence of agony caused by separation of his son (i.e. so killed by you).

verses.sanskrit: हतं कर्णस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्रियं पुत्रं दुरात्मवान् । स्मरतां द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां वचः क्षत्तुश्च मानद ॥१००॥
ततः सुयोधनो दृष्ट्वा हतमाधिरथिं त्वया । निराशो जीविते त्वद्य राज्ये चैव भवत्वरिः ॥१०१॥
verses.english: And then let the enemy Suyodhana, witness in today Adhiratha's son thus fall a victim to your arms, despair of his life and his sovereignty.

verses.sanskrit: एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चाला वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः । कर्णेन भरतश्रेष्ठ पाण्डवानुज्जिहीर्षवः ॥१०२॥
verses.english: Look up yonder, O foremost of the line of Bharata, (and see how) the Panchalas are dropping off from the sharp points of Karna's arrows in their anxiety to rescue the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चालान् द्रौपदेयांश्च धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिनौ । धृष्टद्युम्नतनूजांश्च शतानीकं च नाकुलिम् ॥१०३॥
verses.english: Know it for certain that the Panchalas, the sons of Draupadi, Dhristadyumna, Shikhandin and the sons of Dhristadyumna and Shatanika, the of Nakula (himself), Sahadeva, Durmukha, Janamejaya and Sudhurman and Satyaki, are held in subjection by Karna. son

verses.sanskrit: नकुलं सहदेवं च दुर्मुखं जनमेजयम् । सुधर्माणं सात्यकिं च विद्धि कर्णवशं गतान् ॥१०४॥
अभ्याहतानां कर्णेन पञ्चालानामसौ रणे । श्रूयते निनदो घोरस्त्वद्बन्धूनां परन्तप ॥१०५॥
verses.english: (From off the scene of action) the howling groans, O subduer of foes, of those allies of yours, the Panchalas-reach our ears, as they are assailed, in that dreadful engagement with the weapons of Karna.

verses.sanskrit: न त्वेव भीताः पञ्चालाः कथंचित्स्युः पराङ्मुखाः । न हि मृत्युं महेष्वासा गणयन्ति महारणे ॥१०६॥
verses.english: The Panchalas are not the persons to get frightened, much less to show their back in the thick of the fray. In sanguinary battle these mighty wielders of bow do not at all care to stake their life.

verses.sanskrit: य एकः पाण्डवीं सेनां शरौघैः समवेष्टयत् । तं समासाद्य पञ्चाला भीष्मान्नासन्पराङ्गुखाः ॥१०७॥
verses.english: The Panchalas did not show their back even encountering redoubtable Bhishma, who, alone and unaided, hemmed in the Pandava forces with a thick cloud of shafts.

verses.sanskrit: ते कथं कर्णमासाद्य विद्रवेयुर्महारथाः । यस्त्वेकः सर्वपञ्चालानहन्यहनि नाशयन् ॥१०८॥
verses.english: O benevolent friend! Panchala always kept on fighting in support of Pandavas when they found Dronacharya came for battle irrespective of Drona's march fiercely like death god in the chariot-rode army of Panchala killing them severally, whose face glew in the light of friction in weapons, who was preceptor to all archers and disastrous for the army of enemy in battle-field viz.. they did not shown back to battle-field and put at stake their lives for the cause of Pandavas. O enemy suppressor Arjuna! It is the main characteristic of Panchala soldiers that they are always prepared to defeat the enemies. They cannot show back to battle-field under fright of Karna, the son of a charioteer.

verses.sanskrit: कालवच्चरते वीरः पञ्चालानां रथव्रजे । तमप्यासाद्य समरे मित्रार्थे मित्रवत्सल ॥१०९॥
तथा ज्वलन्तमस्त्राग्निं गुरुं सर्वधनुष्मताम् । निर्दहन्तं च समरे दुर्धर्षं द्रोणमोजसा ॥११०॥
ते नित्यमुदिता जेतुं मृधे शत्रूनरिंदम । न जात्वाधिरथेर्भीताः पञ्चालाः स्युः पराङ्मुखाः ॥१११॥
तेषामापततां शूरः पञ्चालानां तरस्विनाम् । आदत्तासूञ्शरैः कर्णः पतङ्गानामिवानलः ॥११२॥
verses.english: Like the flaming fire consuming myriads of insects that irrepressible Karna with his shafts devoured these swift-armed. Panchalas as they approached him in battle array.

verses.sanskrit: एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चाला द्राव्यन्ते योधिभिर्ध्रुवम् । कर्णेन भरतश्रेष्ठ पश्य पश्य तथाकृतान् ॥११३॥
verses.english: O Bharata! See here, these Panchala warriors racing. Karna and other warriors are so making them to run so haphazard. Look there, they are trapped in a worst network.

verses.sanskrit: तांस्तथाऽभिमुखान्वीरान्मित्रार्थे त्यक्तजीवितान् । क्षयं नयति राधेयः पञ्चालाञ्छतशो रणे ॥११४॥
verses.english: Rallying round the banner of their allies as these valiant Panchalas, reckless of their life, marched against him the son of Radha took off their hordes by legions.

verses.sanskrit: तद्भारत महेष्वासानगाधे मज्जतोऽप्लवे । कर्णार्णवे प्लवो भूत्वा पञ्चालांस्त्रातुमर्हसि ॥११५॥
verses.english: O Bharata, it now behoves you to steer these sturdy bowmen, the valiant Panchala forces, who are fast sinking in the ocean of Karna without a bark.

verses.sanskrit: अस्त्रं हि रामात्कर्णेन भार्गवादृषिसत्तमात् । यदुपात्तं महाघोरं तस्य रूपमुदीर्यते ॥११६॥
verses.english: The weapon which Karna obtained from that foremost sage Rama, the son of Bhrigu, is blazing forth its appalling form.

verses.sanskrit: तापनं सर्वसैन्यानां घोररूपं सुदारुणम् । समावृत्य महासेनां ज्वलन्तं स्वेन तेजसा ॥११७॥
verses.english: The awful form of that weapon, spreading terror and consternation all round and encompassing the vast array of troops, is glistening with its own bright.

verses.sanskrit: एते चरन्ति संग्रामे कर्णचापच्युताः शराः । भ्रमराणामिव व्रातास्तापयन्ति स्म तावकान् ॥११८॥
verses.english: Those arrows flung from the bow-strings of Kamna, afflicting your hosts in battle, are hovering round like swarms of bees.

verses.sanskrit: एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चाला दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत । कर्णास्त्रं समरे प्राप्य दुर्निवार्यमनात्मभिः ॥११९॥
verses.english: Afflicting in battle with the shots of Karna, that is irresistible by persons of weak nerve, O Bharata, the Panchalas, are flying in all directions.

verses.sanskrit: एष भीमो दृढक्रोधो वृतः पार्थ समन्ततः । सृञ्जयैर्योधयन्कर्णं पीड्यते निशितैः शरैः ॥१२०॥
verses.english: Yonder, O Partha, foaming and frothing with rage yet unsatiated, fights Bhima with the Srinjaya forces around him and is getting afflicted with the sharp arrows of Karna.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डवान्सृञ्जयांश्चैव पञ्चालांश्चैव भारत । हन्यादुपेक्षितः कर्णो रोगो देहमिवागतः ॥१२१॥
verses.english: O Bharata, if you remain indifferent towards Karna, he will cause a sad havoc of the Pandava, the Srinjaya and the Panchala forces, like the seizure of the ills, that flesh is heir to, makes the body succumb.

verses.sanskrit: नान्यं त्वत्तो हि पश्यामि योधं यौधिष्ठिरे बले । यः समासाद्य राधेयं स्वस्तिमानाव्रजेद्गृहम् ॥१२२॥
verses.english: Amongst the vast array of the forces of Yudhishthira, I find not another general, save and beyond yourself, who is capable of returning from the field scatheless, after having encountered son of Radha in battle.

verses.sanskrit: तमद्य निशितैर्बाणैर्विनिहत्य नरर्षभ । यथाप्रतिज्ञं पार्थ त्वं कृत्वा कीर्तिमवाप्नुहि ॥१२३॥
verses.english: O foremost of men, buckle on your armour, therefore, to pop off Karna with the keen shafts of your arrows and thus redeeming your pledge, redound your glory.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं सकर्णानपि कौरवान् । नान्यो युधि युधां श्रेष्ठ सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ॥१२४॥
verses.english: Most assuredly I tell you, O warrior of warriors, you and you alone, are capable of worsting Karna in battle and defeating the whole bands of Kaurava army.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्कृत्वा महत्कर्म हत्वा कर्णं महारथम् । कृतार्थः सफलः पार्थ सुखी भव नरोत्तम ॥१२५॥
verses.english: And accomplishing this proud feat, O Partha and achieving victory over the master car-warrior, Karna, may you, the best of men, gain your ends and be successful and happy.
